LESSON: WRITING 13.4.1 SPELLING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.4: Writing 13.4.1 Spelling
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 13.4.1 Spelling, part of Strand 13 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we write words correctly? 2. Which words have the same pronunciation but different spelling?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify homophones, words with double consonants such as slipped, clapping, carefully and words with double vowels from a text,

2. listen to words read by the teacher or from audio recording for example: - waist/waste - collect/dropped

3. write down words from a dictation correctly,

4. use a jigsaw puzzle to form words correctly with peers,

5. make words from jumbled up letters,

6. form sentences from the words they have spelt, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify homophones, words with double consonants such as slipped, clapping, carefully and words with double vowels from a text,
2. listen to words read by the teacher or from audio recording for example: - waist/waste - collect/dropped
3. write down words from a dictation correctly,
4. use a jigsaw puzzle to form words correctly with peers,
5. make words from jumbled up letters,
6. form sentences from the words they have spelt, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 13.4.1 Spelling together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and problem solving is enhanced as the learner makes words from jumbled up letters.

• Learning to Learn is fostered as learners build on their own learning when searching for homophones, words with

double consonants and words with double vowels from the internet.

Values:
Unity is developed as the learner creates puzzles and rearranges jumbled up sentences collaboratively with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Financial literacy is enhanced as the learner interacts with vocabulary about money.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies the skill of proper spelling in all learning areas especially Kiswahili.

APPENDIX 2: COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING

GUIDELINES FOR GRADE 5 COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING PROJECT

Introduction

There will be one integrated Community Service Learning activity that will be conducted annually for Grade 5

learners. The thematic areas for the integrated CSL activity will be derived from the broader categories of the PCIs and

will incorporate concepts from the various Learning Areas. Teachers are expected to vary the themes each year to allow

learners to address different PCIs within their contexts. A clear linkage should exist between the skills from the

learning areas and the chosen themes.

The integrated CSL activity will employ a Whole School Approach (WS
A) involving the entire school community

including learners, parents/caregivers/guardians, school administration and teachers. Parents/caregivers/guardians are

key stakeholders in planning and execution of the CSL activity. While the teacher takes the lead role in planning and

integrating the CSL activity, learners are expected to actively participate throughout the process.

The CSL activity provides an opportunity for the development of core competencies and the nurturing of various

values. The teacher is expected to vary the core competencies and values emphasised in the activity annually.

114

Steps in carrying out the integrated CSL activity

1) Preparation


  -  Determine the activity for the learners


  -  Map out the targeted core competencies, values and specific learning areas skills for the CSL activity


  -  Identify resources required for the activity (locally available material
s) 
  -  Stagger the activities across the term (set dates and time for the activitie
s) 
  -  Communicate to learners, parents/caregivers/guardians, school administration, teachers and other relevant

stakeholders in the school community


  -  Identify and develop assessment tools

2) Implementation of CSL Activity


  -  Assigning roles to learners.


  -  Ensure every learner actively participates in the activity


  -  Observe learners as they carry out the CSL activity and record feedback.


  -  Use an appropriate assessment tool to assess both the process and the product (assess learner’s work from the

beginning to the end produc
t) 
  -  Assess the targeted core competencies, values and subject skills.

3) Reflection on the CSL Activity

Conduct a self-evaluation session with learners on the integrated CSL activity undertaken by discussing the

following:


  -  what went well and why?


  -  what did not go well and why?


  -  what can be done differently next time?


  -  what they have learnt?

115

ASSESSMENT OF CSL INTEGRATED PROJECT

Assessment of the integrated CSL activity will focus on 3 components namely: skills from various learning areas

applied in carrying out the activity, core competencies developed and values nurtured. Assessment should focus on

both the process and end product of the CSL activity. The teacher will assess learners in groups using various tools

such as observation schedules, checklists, rating scales or any other appropriate assessment tool.

116
